target_moa.text: CNS-penetrant tyrosine kinase inhibitor of ROS1 (including resistance mutations G2032R, L1951R, L2026M, D2033N) with activity against TRK A/B/C; inhibits growth of cancer cells expressing ROS1 fusion genes and mutations

citations.quote: Taletrectinib is a CNS-penetrant inhibitor of proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase ROS1, including *ROS1* resistance mutations G2032R, L1951R, L2026M, and D2033N. Taletrectinib also showed inhibitory effects on tropomyosin receptor kinase (TRK) A/B/C, with approximately 11- to 20-fold selectivity over TRKB.

Fusion proteins that include ROS1 domains can drive tumorigenic potential through hyperactivation of downstream signaling pathways leading to unconstrained cell proliferation. Taletrectinib inhibited growth of cancer cells expressing *ROS1* fusion genes and mutations.
Pharmacologic Class	Kinase inhibitor
IBTROZI is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1 rearrangement(s) (2,3).

key_safety.text: Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions: diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, rash, constipation, fatigue. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 31% of patients (pneumonia 7%, pleural effusion 4.7%, hepatotoxicity 2.4%); fatal adverse reactions in 18 (5%) patients. Warnings include hepatotoxicity (AST increased in 88%, ALT increased in 85%), ILD/pneumonitis, and QTc prolongation

citations.quote: In this pooled safety population, the most common (\ge 20\%) adverse reactions were diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, rash, constipation, and fatigue.

Serious adverse reactions occurred in 31% of patients who received IBTROZI. Serious adverse reactions in \ge 2\% of patients included pneumonia (7%), pleural effusion (4.7%), and hepatotoxicity (2.4%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 18 (5%) patients who received IBTROZI

based on laboratory values, 88% of patients treated with IBTROZI experienced increased aspartate aminotransferase (AST), including 10% Grade 3 or 4. Increased alanine aminotransferase (ALT) occurred in 85% of patients treated with IBTROZI, including 13% Grade 3 or 4.

In the pooled safety population [*see Adverse Reactions (6.1)*], interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis occurred in 2.3% of patients treated with IBTROZI, including Grade 3 or 4 in 1.1% of patients. The median time to first onset of ILD/pneumonitis was 3.8 months (range: 12 days to 11.8 months).

IBTROZI can cause QTc interval prolongation, which can increase the risk for ventricular tachyarrhythmias (e.g., torsades de pointes) or sudden death. IBTROZI prolongs the QTc interval in a concentration-dependent manner [*see Clinical Pharmacology (12.2)*].

detail.text: Patients are selected based on ROS1 rearrangement(s) in tumor specimens, but no FDA-approved test for ROS1 rearrangement selection is currently available; local labs used NGS, PCR, FISH, or IHC

citations.quote: An FDA-approved test to detect *ROS1* rearrangement(s) for selecting patients for treatment with IBTROZI is not currently available.

Identification of *ROS1* gene fusions in tumor specimens was determined in local laboratories using next-generation sequencing (NGS), polymerase chain reaction (PCR), fluorescence in situ (FISH), or immunohistochemistry (IHC).
